Isolated-apply branch prefix, asserted on `result.details.branchName` and on the merge-failure notice. The prefix is how a conflicted branch is identified back to the task that created it, including from inside an error message the user reads.

The `omp://` scheme the internal filesystem serves rendered documentation from, asserted on ReadDir results, symlink targets and a generated URL. A tool resolves the scheme to decide it is reading the doc tree rather than the working directory, so it is the primary key of the virtual filesystem.

The two commands the startup error names: the one that starts the broker and the one that resets its URL. Both are asserted with toContain because the user is expected to run them verbatim, so the command line is the contract.

Plugin subcommands the launch guard redirects to — `omp plugin list`, `omp plugin uninstall`, `omp plugin marketplace`. Each occurrence names a command the user can type, including from the doc comment that records why the guard exists; the test is asserting the suggestion text a user is handed, not the brand.

The `omp:sessions:file:` Redis key prefix the session store reads back. The prefix partitions this product's keys inside a shared Redis, so it is a wire namespace with a live reader rather than a string the fixture happened to choose.

The `omp:sessions:file:` and `omp:sessions:meta` Redis key prefixes the store reads, asserts and writes across resume, rename, delete and peer-replication paths. Every occurrence is a key the implementation itself must resolve, asserted on `redis.strings.get(...)`, so the namespace is the contract under test.

The `omp://share/` and `omp:` share-URL forms that must be kept out of persisted shell history. The scheme is how a shared session is addressed by another user, so the test pins the prefix that identifies it — matching the form, not the shared id.

The upgrade command the update-available line tells the user to run, asserted inside an exact toEqual on the rendered lines. The whole line is compared, so the command is part of the string contract the renderer must reproduce byte for byte.

The `omp://` documentation URLs grep returns and expands, asserted on rendered text and on `result.details.files`. The scheme is what separates a virtual doc path from a working-directory one, so grep resolves it before deciding how to report a hit.

The `omp://` doc URLs the renderer turns a find hit into, asserted on `uris` including the `:10` line-anchor form. The URL is what makes the hit clickable, so the scheme and its anchor shape are the contract between the search result and the terminal.

The `omp --resume <session>` command the recovery notice prints when cleanup fails. The user copies that command to recover the session, so the assertion is on an invocation that must stay runnable, not on a message that merely reads well.
